description: Capture-profile registry (STO-SCN-091). Keyed on {make, model, mode}; maps a camera + capture mode to the COLMAP camera model and solver compatibility. The camera model is a property of the camera/capture mode, NOT the scene (STO-SCN-096 conclusion #3) — so it is decided here from known capture metadata, never inferred from pixels. `mode` (fisheye vs dewarped) is NOT carried in EXIF on DJI footage and must be declared per scene.
sources: HUG-SCN-004 (Validated capture profile + COLMAP/SLAM capture pitfalls)

profiles.notes: Native 155° fisheye. Reconstructs the distortion directly; COLMAP needs SIMPLE_RADIAL_FISHEYE (PINHOLE/OPENCV fail). Validated capture profile: 2.7K@30fps, locked exposure/WB, stable motion. Hyperlapse cadence is a separate solver-routing concern (STO-SCN-093): COLMAP sequential matcher fails on hyperlapse — use SLAM/feed-forward there even though the camera MODEL is unchanged.

In-camera-dewarped video does NOT reconstruct in COLMAP under ANY camera model (002 dead-end, corroborated by the 001 capture notes). Route to SLAM / feed-forward only. Reconciled from STO-SCN-096 conclusion #3 (which said OPENCV) to match HUG-SCN-004's stronger 'COLMAP-incompatible' verdict, 2026-06-13.

iPhone main camera is natively rectilinear (well-corrected, mild residual radial). Routes via the pinhole/rectilinear path (solve_plan): FastMap directly, NO fisheye undistort; SIMPLE_RADIAL lets the solver SELF-ESTIMATE the residual radial term, so no per-lens calibration block is required (unlike the DJI fisheye). single_camera assumes ONE locked lens per capture (don't mix 0.5x/1x/3x in a scene). PROVISIONAL: validated by the solve (T-020); refine the model only if poses degrade.
profiles.source: STO-SCN-091/093; provisional — added to unblock 007-kubota (iPhone capture)
